title: Supplemental regional records for previously empty information categories
policy: Records are named examples with source links, not exhaustive inventories. Category coverage is not equivalent to complete 36-region coverage. Expand only after region-specific source verification.

records.name: Pranahita
records.description: The Pranhita is part of the Godavari basin and meets the Godavari at Kaleshwaram on the Andhra Pradesh–Maharashtra border. The CWC identifies the Pranhita sub-basin and its principal tributary system.
records.referenceDate: CWC Assessment of Water Resources of India, 2024

records.name: Subansiri
records.description: The CWC identifies the Subansiri as a principal right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra. The Brahmaputra basin includes Assam; CWC hydrological monitoring also lists Subansiri stations in Lakhimpur, Assam.
records.referenceDate: CWC Assessment of Water Resources of India, 2024

records.name: Kosi
records.description: The CWC identifies the Kosi as the largest tributary of the Ganga, notes its Himalayan headwaters, and describes it as the 'sorrow of Bihar' because of its recurrent floods.
records.referenceDate: CWC Assessment of Water Resources of India, 2024

records.name: Teesta
records.description: The CWC identifies the Teesta as a principal right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra. Its basin assessment includes West Bengal within the Indian Brahmaputra basin.
records.referenceDate: CWC Assessment of Water Resources of India, 2024

records.name: Ib River
records.description: Odisha's Department of Water Resources lists Ib among the major tributaries of the Mahanadi in the State; CWC's Mahanadi Water Year Book identifies Ib as a major left-bank tributary and records its drainage through Sundargarh, Jharsuguda and Sambalpur.
records.referenceDate: Official State/Central government source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Yamuna
records.description: The Prayagraj District Administration identifies the Yamuna as one of the district's two main rivers and states that it meets the Ganga at Prayagraj Sangam in Uttar Pradesh.
records.referenceDate: Official State/Central government source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Jog Falls
records.description: Jog Falls is formed by the Sharavathi River and is located in Sagar Taluk, Shivamogga district, Karnataka.
records.referenceDate: Official State/UT or district government page accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Nohkalikai Falls
records.description: Nohkalikai Falls is located in East Khasi Hills district, approximately 7.5 km from Sohra (Cherrapunji), Meghalaya.
records.referenceDate: Official State/UT or district government page accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Dudhsagar Falls
records.description: Dudhsagar Waterfalls is located in Sanguem taluka, Goa, on the Goa–Karnataka border in the Mandovi river system.
records.referenceDate: Official State/UT or district government page accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Athirappilly Falls
records.description: Athirappilly Falls is in Athirappilly Panchayat, Chalakudy Taluk, Thrissur district, Kerala, on the Chalakudy River.
records.referenceDate: Official State/UT or district government page accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Hundru Falls
records.description: Hundru Falls is formed on the Subarnarekha (Swarnarekha) River near Ranchi, Jharkhand.
records.referenceDate: Official State/UT or district government page accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Hogenakkal Falls
records.description: Hogenakkal Falls is on the Cauvery River, approximately 45 km from Dharmapuri, Tamil Nadu.
records.referenceDate: Official State/UT or district government page accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Deccan Trap basalt province
records.description: The Geological Survey of India describes the Deccan Trap lava province as extending mainly across Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh; the record denotes its Madhya Pradesh occurrence.
records.referenceDate: Geological Survey of India geological profiles and atlas accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Chota Nagpur Gneissic Complex
records.description: The Jharkhand Space Applications Center's Ranchi District soil resources report maps the Chota-Nagpur Gneissic Complex across parts of the district and describes its granite, gneiss, phyllite and mica-schist terrain.
records.referenceDate: Official State/Central government source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Aravalli fold belt
records.description: GSI's Rajasthan geology profile describes the Aravalli Supergroup and Aravalli Fold Belt within the State's Precambrian geological provinces.
records.referenceDate: Geological Survey of India geological profiles and atlas accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Shillong Plateau basement complex
records.description: GSI's Meghalaya geology profile identifies the Precambrian Gneissic Complex and overlying Shillong Group of sedimentary rocks as major geological units of the State.
records.referenceDate: Geological Survey of India geological profiles and atlas accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Eastern Ghats granulite belt
records.description: GSI's Odisha geology profile describes the Eastern Ghat Mobile Belt and its granulite-facies lithoassemblages, including khondalite, charnockite and mafic granulites.
records.referenceDate: Geological Survey of India geological profiles and atlas accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Kachchh sedimentary basin
records.description: GSI's Gujarat geology profile identifies the Kachchh region's Mesozoic sedimentary formations, including the Pachchham, Chari, Katrol and Bhuj formations.
records.referenceDate: Geological Survey of India geological profiles and atlas accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Chhattisgarh Basin
records.description: GSI records siliceous tuff beds in the basal sedimentary sequence of the Chhattisgarh Basin, supporting the named Proterozoic intracratonic basin entry.
records.referenceDate: Geological Survey of India geological profiles and atlas accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Deccan volcanic province
records.description: The Geological Survey of India describes the Deccan Trap lava province as extending mainly across Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh; the record denotes its Maharashtra occurrence.
records.referenceDate: Geological Survey of India geological profiles and atlas accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Chandrapur Super Thermal Power Station
records.description: Chandrapur Super Thermal Power Station is operated by Maharashtra State Power Generation Company Limited at Urjanagar, Chandrapur, Maharashtra.
records.referenceDate: Official generating-company source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Rihand Super Thermal Power Station
records.description: NTPC's Rihand thermal power station is located at Rihandnagar, Sonbhadra district, Uttar Pradesh.
records.referenceDate: Official generating-company source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Vindhyachal Super Thermal Power Station
records.description: NTPC's official coal-station register lists Vindhyachal in Madhya Pradesh and gives its commissioned capacity; this record identifies the station, not a live output figure.
records.referenceDate: Official generating-company source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Korba Super Thermal Power Station
records.description: NTPC's official coal-station register lists Korba in Chhattisgarh and gives its commissioned capacity; this record identifies the station, not a live output figure.
records.referenceDate: Official generating-company source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ramagundam Super Thermal Power Station
records.description: NTPC's Ramagundam thermal power station is located in Telangana; the operator lists its installed capacity and unit configuration.
records.referenceDate: Official generating-company source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Talcher Super Thermal Power Station
records.description: NTPC Talcher Kaniha is located in Angul district, Odisha; the operator lists its approved capacity and commissioned unit stages.
records.referenceDate: Official generating-company source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: North Chennai Thermal Power Station
records.description: The Central Electricity Authority's list of thermal power stations as of 31 March 2023 records North Chennai TPS under TANGEDCO in the Tamil Nadu state sector, with its commissioned units.
records.referenceDate: Official State/Central government source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Farakka Super Thermal Power Station
records.description: NTPC's official coal-station register lists Farakka in West Bengal and gives its commissioned capacity; this record identifies the station, not a live output figure.
records.referenceDate: Official generating-company source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Mundra Thermal Power Station
records.description: Adani Power's FY 2024-25 operational report identifies Mundra as a coal-based thermal power plant in Gujarat and reports its cumulative capacity.
records.referenceDate: Official generating-company source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Visakhapatnam industrial and port cluster
records.description: The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation identifies Visakhapatnam as an industrial city with steel, petroleum, fertilizers, shipbuilding, heavy engineering, port activity and pharma/IT zones.
records.referenceDate: Official State industrial development authority / municipal source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ahmedabad–Sanand industrial region
records.description: GIDC's current industrial-estate register lists multiple Ahmedabad estates and Sanand industrial estates, supporting the Ahmedabad–Sanand manufacturing concentration.
records.referenceDate: Official State industrial development authority / municipal source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Mumbai–Pune industrial corridor
records.description: MIDC identifies Mumbai–Thane–Raigad and Pune–Chakan–Talegaon–Satara as major industrial land-bank regions with engineering, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, food processing and auto-component sectors; these are related industrial belts, not a single formally designated corridor.
records.referenceDate: Official State industrial development authority / municipal source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Chennai–Sriperumbudur industrial region
records.description: SIPCOT lists Sriperumbudur Industrial Park and SEZ, Oragadam and Irungattukottai industrial parks in Kancheepuram district, establishing the Chennai–Sriperumbudur industrial concentration.
records.referenceDate: Official State industrial development authority / municipal source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Bengaluru technology and manufacturing cluster
records.description: Invest Karnataka describes Bengaluru Urban as a technology and industrial hub with large- and medium-scale industries across IT, biotechnology, aerospace and food processing, and identifies Peenya as a major industrial cluster.
records.referenceDate: Official State industrial development authority / municipal source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Kolkata–Haldia economic region
records.description: West Bengal Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation identifies Haldia as an industrial hub with port-linked chemicals, petrochemicals, manufacturing and logistics, located in Purba Medinipur.
records.referenceDate: Official State industrial development authority / municipal source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Magadha
records.description: The Government of Bihar's tourism history identifies Magadha as a major ancient power centred first at Rajgir and later at Pataliputra (modern Patna).
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Kosala
records.description: The Ayodhya District Administration identifies Ayodhya as the capital of the ancient Kosala Kingdom; the Lucknow district history also places Ayodhya and later Shravasti within the Kosala tradition.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Satavahana polity
records.description: NCERT's state profile for Andhra Pradesh records the long rule of the Satavahana dynasty in the region and identifies Gautamiputra Satakarni as a major second-century CE ruler.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Western Chalukyas of Kalyani
records.description: An ASI epigraphical record identifies the Chalukyas of Kalyani and a copper-plate inscription of Tailapa II dated 975 CE, supporting the dynasty's Karnataka association.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Imperial Cholas
records.description: ASI's monument history records 10th-century Chola inscriptions and later Chola-period records in Tamil Nadu, including donations and temple administration.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ahom kingdom
records.description: Assam Tourism records Chaolung Sukapha's arrival in the 13th century and the Ahom kingdom's rule over much of the Brahmaputra Valley for around 600 years, ending in the early 19th century.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Kingdom of Manipur
records.description: Manipur Tourism records a long history of kingship in Manipur dating to 33 CE and identifies the state's historic kingdom, heritage sites and royal-era monuments.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Partition of Bengal (1905) and Swadeshi movement
records.description: The Government of India's Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav history page documents Vande Mataram's role in the 1905 anti-partition protests in Calcutta, a central expression of the Swadeshi mobilisation.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919)
records.description: The Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Act, 1951 identifies the killings and injuries at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar on 13 April 1919 and establishes the national memorial.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Quit India Movement (1942)
records.description: The Government of India's Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav district archive identifies the Quit India 1942 event in Central Mumbai, Maharashtra, supporting Bombay's role in the movement's launch.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Champaran Satyagraha (1917)
records.description: The Gandhi Heritage Portal's event chronology documents Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha from April 1917 onward, with dated events in Motihari, Bettiah and other locations in Bihar.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Quit India movement in Assam
records.description: The Government of India's freedom-movement archive documents the 20 September 1942 Quit India processions and police firing at Dhekiajuli and Gohpur in Assam, including Kanaklata Barua.
records.referenceDate: Official government history, heritage or archival source accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Rabindranath Tagore — Gitanjali
records.description: NobelPrize.org lists Gitanjali (Song Offerings) among Tagore's selected works and records his 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature; Tagore was born in Calcutta, Bengal.
records.referenceDate: Nobel Prize / Sahitya Akademi official archive accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Assamese Sahitya Akademi award tradition
records.description: Sahitya Akademi's Assamese-language award archive (1955–2025) records award-winning books and authors, including the 2025 award to Devabrat Das for Karhi Khelar Sadhu.
records.referenceDate: Nobel Prize / Sahitya Akademi official archive accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Tamil Sahitya Akademi award archive
records.description: Sahitya Akademi's Tamil-language award archive (1955–2025) records award-winning books and authors, including the 2025 award to Sa. Tamilselvan for Thamiz Sirukathaiyin Thadangal.
records.referenceDate: Nobel Prize / Sahitya Akademi official archive accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Malayalam Sahitya Akademi award archive
records.description: Sahitya Akademi's Malayalam-language award archive (1955–2025) records award-winning books and authors, including the 2025 award to N. Prabhakaran for Maayaamanushyar.
records.referenceDate: Nobel Prize / Sahitya Akademi official archive accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Manipuri Sahitya Akademi award archive
records.description: Sahitya Akademi's Manipuri-language award archive (since 1973) records award-winning books and authors, including the 2025 award to Haobam Nalini for Kanglamdriba Eephut.
records.referenceDate: Nobel Prize / Sahitya Akademi official archive accessed 31 October 2026

records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry for the marble gorge and geological landscape along the Narmada.

records.name: Salkhan Fossil Park, Sonbhadra
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry for fossil-bearing geological formations at Salkhan.

records.name: Naga Hill Ophiolite
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry for ophiolitic rocks and tectonic geology in the Naga Hills.

records.name: Natural Heritage of Varkala
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry for the coastal cliff and associated geological formations at Varkala.

records.name: Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry for the Baratang karst and mud-volcano landscape.

records.name: Andaman Subduction Volcanoes
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry for volcanic features associated with the Andaman subduction zone.

records.name: Udaigiri Caves
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry added 8 July 2026 for the rock-cut cave complex at Udaigiri near Vidisha.

records.name: Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley: Bateshwar, Padavali and Kakarmath
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry added 8 July 2026 for the temple group in the Chambal Valley.

records.name: Ginnorgarh Fort
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry added 8 July 2026 for the historic fort of Ginnorgarh.

records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry added 19 June 2026 for the historic ensemble associated with the Ahom capital region at Sivasagar.

records.name: The Painted Haveli Towns of Shekhawati
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry added 1 June 2026 for the painted havelis and historic merchant towns of Shekhawati.

records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry added 22 May 2026 documenting the cultural continuity of Nicobarese communities.

records.name: Colonial Penal Settlement of Andaman Islands
records.description: UNESCO Tentative List entry added 22 May 2026 concerning the colonial penal settlement history of the Andaman Islands.

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Brahmaputra tributaries in Arunachal Pradesh: Dibang and Lohit. The Brahmaputra enters India near Sadiya and receives both as left-bank tributaries.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Brahmaputra tributaries through the Assam valley include Burhi Dihing and Dhansari (south bank), and Subansiri, Kameng, Manas and Sankosh (right bank).
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Jhelum is an important tributary of the Indus, rising at Verinag in the Kashmir Valley. The wider Indus system also includes the Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Indus receives Himalayan tributaries in the Ladakh region including Shyok, Zaskar, Nubra, Shigar, Gasting and Dras, as listed in NCERT's Indus System account.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Chenab is formed by the Chandra and Bhaga streams joining at Tandi; the Ravi and Beas also rise in Himachal Pradesh and join the Indus system.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Beas meets the Sutlej near Harike. NCERT identifies the Panjnad as the combined waters of the Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab and Jhelum in the Indus system.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Alaknanda system includes the Dhauli and Vishnu Ganga, with the Pindar joining at Karna Prayag and the Mandakini (Kali Ganga) joining at Rudra Prayag.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Yamuna tributaries include Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken on the right bank, and Hindan, Rind, Sengar and Varuna on the left. Ramganga and Gomati are also Ganga tributaries.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Major Ganga tributaries entering or flowing through Bihar include the Son, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Mahananda is a left-bank tributary of the Ganga in West Bengal. The Damodar joins the Hugli; Barakar is the main tributary of the Damodar.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Barakar is the main tributary of the Damodar, which flows along the eastern margins of the Chota Nagpur Plateau.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Chambal rises near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh, flows through Rajasthan including the Kota region, and finally joins the Yamuna.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken are Yamuna tributaries; the Son rises in the Amarkantak Plateau and joins the Ganga.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Godavari tributaries include Penganga, Wainganga, Wardha (together forming Pranhita), Indravati, Sabari and Manjra. Krishna tributaries include Koyna, Ghatprabha, Malprabha and Bhima.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Manjira and Pranahita systems feed the Godavari; the Bhima and Tungabhadra are tributaries of the Krishna system. The NCERT text notes shared river systems across Telangana and neighbouring States.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Krishna tributaries include Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Bhima and Tungabhadra. Kaveri tributaries include Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkavathy, Kabini, Bhavani, Noyyal and Amaravati.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Krishna and Godavari river systems and their tributaries drain the State; NCERT identifies shared tributary systems across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Kaveri tributaries include Bhavani, Noyyal and Amaravati; the State's river systems also include the Vaigai and Tamraparni basins.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Magadha, Anga and Vajji Mahajanapadas
records.description: NCERT identifies Magadha as the most powerful mahajanapada, with early capital Rajagaha (present-day Rajgir) and later capital Pataliputra (present-day Patna). The map also places Anga at Champa and Vajji at Vaishali.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Kosala, Kashi, Vatsa, Panchala, Malla and Shurasena Mahajanapadas
records.description: NCERT's map of early states places Kosala at Shravasti, Kashi at Varanasi, Vatsa at Kaushambi, Panchala at Ahichchhatra, Malla at Kusinagara and Shurasena at Mathura.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Avanti Mahajanapada
records.description: NCERT's map of early states identifies Avanti with its capital at Ujjayini (present-day Ujjain).
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Matsya Mahajanapada
records.description: NCERT's map of early states places Matsya around Bairat in the present-day Rajasthan region.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Kuru Mahajanapada
records.description: NCERT's map of early states identifies Indraprastha as the Kuru capital, in the present-day Delhi region.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Vanga Mahajanapada
records.description: NCERT's map of early states identifies Vanga in the Bengal region; the historical region extended beyond present-day State boundaries.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Kalinga Kingdom
records.description: NCERT identifies Kalinga as present-day coastal Odisha and notes its conquest by Ashoka.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Chola, Chera and Pandya Chiefdoms of Tamilakam
records.description: NCERT describes the Chola, Chera and Pandya chiefdoms in ancient Tamilakam, the ancient Tamil country.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Chera Chiefdoms of Tamilakam
records.description: NCERT describes the Cheras among the chiefdoms of ancient Tamilakam, which included parts of present-day Kerala as well as Tamil Nadu.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Gurjara-Pratihara Kingdom
records.description: NCERT identifies the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty as a major regional power and places its kingdom in Gujarat and Rajasthan.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Gurjara-Pratihara Kingdom
records.description: NCERT identifies the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty as a major regional power and places its kingdom in Gujarat and Rajasthan.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Chahamana (Chauhan) Kingdom
records.description: NCERT states that the Chahamanas, later known as Chauhans, ruled the region around Delhi and Ajmer.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Chahamana (Chauhan) Kingdom
records.description: NCERT states that the Chahamanas, later known as Chauhans, ruled the region around Delhi and Ajmer.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Rashtrakuta Kingdom
records.description: NCERT describes the Rashtrakutas as a major power in the Deccan; the chapter identifies their rule in the western Deccan.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Rashtrakuta Kingdom
records.description: NCERT describes the Rashtrakutas as a major power in the Deccan; the dynasty's rise followed its subordination to the Chalukyas of Karnataka.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Chalukya Kingdom
records.description: NCERT identifies the Chalukyas of Karnataka as the overlords of the early Rashtrakutas.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Kadamba Kingdom
records.description: NCERT states that Mayurasharman established the Kadamba kingdom in Karnataka.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Pala Kingdom
records.description: NCERT identifies the Palas as a major dynasty in Bengal and one of the parties in the tripartite struggle for Kannauj.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Chola Kingdom
records.description: NCERT identifies the Cholas as rulers of Tamil Nadu; the dynasty rose from Uraiyur and captured the Kaveri delta.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Pallava Kingdom
records.description: NCERT identifies the Pallavas of Kanchipuram as rulers to whom the Muttaraiyar chiefs of the Kaveri delta were subordinate.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Muttaraiyar Chiefs
records.description: NCERT identifies the Muttaraiyar as a chiefly family that held power in the Kaveri delta before the Chola rise.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-II, Chapter 2, 2025-26 reprint

records.name: Mauryan Provincial Centre at Ujjayini
records.description: NCERT lists Ujjayini (present-day Ujjain) among the five major political centres of the Mauryan Empire.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Mauryan Provincial Centre at Tosali and Kalinga
records.description: NCERT lists Tosali as a Mauryan provincial centre and identifies Kalinga as present-day coastal Odisha, conquered by Ashoka.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Mauryan Southern Provincial Centre at Suvarnagiri
records.description: NCERT lists Suvarnagiri among the five major political centres of the Mauryan Empire and notes its possible importance for Karnataka's gold-mining region.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Mauryan Inscriptional Region
records.description: NCERT notes that Ashokan inscriptions have been found in present-day Andhra Pradesh, indicating Mauryan reach in the region.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Ashokan Inscription at Kalsi
records.description: NCERT's map of Ashokan inscriptions marks Kalsi in present-day Uttarakhand.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Satavahana Kingdom of the Western Deccan
records.description: NCERT places the Satavahanas among the major early kingdoms of the western and central Deccan; the source describes regional, not modern State, boundaries.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Southern Tamilakam Chiefdoms
records.description: NCERT states that ancient Tamilakam included parts of present-day Andhra Pradesh and Kerala in addition to Tamil Nadu, and was associated with Chola, Chera and Pandya chiefdoms.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I, Theme Two, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Centres of the Revolt of 1857 in North India
records.description: NCERT documents the 1857 uprising at Meerut, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, Bareilly and Faizabad, including Nana Saheb, Begum Hazrat Mahal and Rani Lakshmibai.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-III, Chapter 5

records.name: Delhi in the Revolt of 1857
records.description: Sepoys from Meerut entered Delhi in May 1857, proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as their leader, and held the city until British forces recaptured it in September 1857.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-III, Chapter 5

records.name: Rani Avantibai Lodhi and the Mandla uprising, 1857
records.description: NCERT records that Rani Avantibai Lodhi of Ramgarh in the Mandla region raised and led an army against British administration in 1857; Tantia Tope continued guerrilla resistance in central India.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-III, Chapter 5

records.name: Kunwar Singh and the 1857 uprising
records.description: NCERT records that Kunwar Singh, a zamindar in Bihar, joined rebel sepoys and fought the British for many months.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-III, Chapter 5

records.name: Mangal Pandey at Barrackpore, 1857
records.description: NCERT records that Mangal Pandey attacked his officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 and was hanged.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-III, Chapter 5

records.name: Khurda Uprising of 1817
records.description: NCERT documents the Khurda uprising in south-eastern Odisha as an earlier resistance to colonial policies, predating the 1857 rebellion.
records.referenceDate: NCERT Our Pasts-III, Chapter 5

records.name: Champaran Satyagraha, 1917
records.description: Gandhi's first major satyagraha in India, launched in Champaran to support indigo cultivators against oppressive plantation arrangements.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Kheda Satyagraha, 1918
records.description: Peasant satyagraha in Kheda district demanding suspension of land revenue after crop failure.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ahmedabad Mill Workers' Strike, 1918
records.description: Labour dispute in Ahmedabad in which Gandhi supported textile mill workers seeking a wage increase.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Bardoli Satyagraha, 1928
records.description: Peasant movement in Bardoli against increased land revenue; led by Vallabhbhai Patel.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Dandi March and Salt Satyagraha, 1930
records.description: Gandhi's march from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to break the colonial salt law and launch civil disobedience.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, 13 April 1919
records.description: British troops fired on a gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar; listed by the Government of India's Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav event portal.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Chauri Chaura Incident, 1922
records.description: A violent incident at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district that led Gandhi to suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Quit India Movement launched in Bombay, 1942
records.description: The All India Congress Committee adopted the Quit India resolution at Bombay on 8 August 1942; Gandhi called for mass civil disobedience.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Vaikom Satyagraha, 1924–25
records.description: Non-violent protest in Travancore against restrictions on the use of roads around the Vaikom temple by oppressed castes.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Gandhi's Odisha tour and anti-untouchability campaign, 1934
records.description: Gandhi toured Odisha in 1934 as part of the campaign against untouchability and for Harijan welfare.
records.referenceDate: Official chronology accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Andhra Pradesh cultural profile
records.description: NCERT highlights the Amaravati Stupa, Godavari and Krishna Pushkaralu, Kuchipudi, Telugu devotional literature, Carnatic music, Kalamkari textiles and Kondapalli toys as major cultural features of Andhra Pradesh.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Major festivals of Assam
records.description: NCERT lists Ambubachi Mela, Doljatra, Bheldiya, Me-Dum-Me-Phi, Ali-Ai-Ligang, Baishagu and Rongker among Assam's fairs and festivals, with distinct ritual, agricultural and community traditions.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Folk dance and performance forms of Bihar
records.description: NCERT documents Jiya/Jhijhia, Jata-Jatin Naach, Kamala, Naach of Kathakiya, Salhes, Chaiti and other regional performance traditions in Bihar.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Major tribal communities of Chhattisgarh
records.description: NCERT identifies Gond, Abujmaria, Bisonhorn Maria, Bhatra, Muria, Halba, Parja, Dhurvaa, Korwa, Kawar, Binjwar, Dhanwar, Kamar and Munda communities across the State's regions.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Portuguese rule and liberation of Goa
records.description: NCERT records that Goa remained under Portuguese rule after 1947 and was liberated on 19 December 1961; the date is observed as Goa Liberation Day.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Folk dances of Gujarat
records.description: NCERT documents Gher Nritya, Shikaar Nritya, Thaakarya/Gadhavi/Baacha Nritya, Aagva, Gheriya, Aaleni-Haaleni, Sword Dance and Kaakda Nritya, including their community and regional associations.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Formation of Haryana as a State
records.description: NCERT notes Haryana's ancient history reaching back to Harappan times and its formation as a full-fledged State on 1 November 1966 following the reorganisation of Punjab.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Phulaich and Kullu Dussehra
records.description: NCERT describes Phulaich, the September flower festival especially observed in Kinnaur, and the ten-day Kullu Dussehra celebrated in October.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Traditional arts and crafts of Jharkhand
records.description: NCERT documents Paitkar and Jadopatiya painting, Sohrai and Khovar wall art, Dhokra metalwork, bamboo and wood craft, pottery, lac jewellery and terracotta work.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Major river systems of Arunachal Pradesh
records.description: NCERT identifies the Siang, Tirap, Kameng, Lohit and Subansiri as the State's main rivers; these snow-fed Himalayan rivers form the Brahmaputra system in Assam and divide Arunachal into five river valleys.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Andaman and Nicobar cultural profile
records.description: NCERT describes the islands' indigenous Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, Sentinelese, Nicobarese and Shompen communities; the Nicobari dance and Ossuary Feast; Cellular Jail in Port Blair; and palm-leaf and pandanus crafts.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.name: Chandigarh cultural profile
records.description: NCERT highlights Chandigarh's planned-city design by Le Corbusier, Capitol Complex, Rock Garden created by Nek Chand, Sukhna Lake, Rose Garden, museums, and a lively programme of festivals and performing arts.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Unity in Cultural Diversity, first edition June 2018

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu cultural profile
records.description: NCERT records the territory's four separate geographic components, the Dhodia, Kokna and Varli communities, Damanganga river system, Portuguese heritage in Daman and Diu, and a cultural blend of Gujarati, Marathi, Konkani and tribal traditions.

records.name: South Andaman visitor destinations
records.description: The South Andaman District Administration lists Cellular Jail, Ross Island, Chidiya Tapu and Wandoor among visitor destinations. This is a district-level selection within the wider Andaman and Nicobar Islands, not an exhaustive island-by-island inventory.
records.referenceDate: Official South Andaman district tourism page accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: West Bengal tourism destinations
records.description: West Bengal Tourism highlights destinations including Darjeeling, the Sundarbans, the Dooars, Bishnupur and Kolkata; this is a selected State tourism profile.
records.referenceDate: Official West Bengal Tourism portal accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli tourism destinations
records.description: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli district portal lists visitor sites including Silvassa, Dudhani and Vasona Lion Safari; this record covers the DNH portion of the combined Union Territory.
records.referenceDate: Official Dadra and Nagar Haveli district tourism page accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Daman and Diu tourism destinations
records.description: The Daman and Diu district tourism portals list coastal and heritage destinations including Daman Fort, Jampore Beach, Diu Fort and Naida Caves; this complements the DNH district profile for the combined Union Territory.
records.referenceDate: Official Diu district tourism page accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Delhi tourism destinations
records.description: Delhi Tourism's official destination directory covers major heritage and visitor sites including the Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, Jama Masjid and other city attractions.
records.referenceDate: Official Delhi Tourism destination directory accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Coral bleaching and marine ecosystem stress
records.description: The Ministry of Earth Sciences' 4 December 2024 report records small-scale coral bleaching in the Andaman region, especially South Andaman, associated with elevated sea-surface temperature during the El Niño event.
records.referenceDate: Ministry of Earth Sciences, Lok Sabha answer, 4 December 2024

records.name: Urban heat, air quality and waste-management pressures
records.description: Chandigarh's 2026 Environment Department report addresses urban heat-island effects, air quality, waste and water management and climate adaptation as environmental management priorities for the Union Territory.
records.referenceDate: Chandigarh Environment Department report, 2026

records.name: Cold-desert climate and water-security risks
records.description: MoEFCC's Ladakh SAPCC profile describes warming, changes in snowfall and snow cover, glacier-related concerns, pressure on water availability, fragile mountain ecosystems and the risk of localised cloudburst flash floods.
records.referenceDate: MoEFCC NAPCC Dashboard — Ladakh SAPCC profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Coral bleaching and fragile coastal ecosystems
records.description: The Ministry of Earth Sciences' 4 December 2024 report records widespread coral bleaching in Lakshadweep associated with elevated sea-surface temperature during the El Niño event. The UT Environment Department identifies coral reefs and coastal habitats as sensitive ecosystems requiring monitoring and restoration.
records.referenceDate: Ministry of Earth Sciences, Lok Sabha answer, 4 December 2024

records.name: Coral-reef and marine biodiversity
records.description: The Lakshadweep Environment and Forest Department identifies coral reefs, marine life, sea turtles, humpback whales, the Dr. Salim Ali Pitti Bird Sanctuary, marine wildlife reserves and medicinal-plant conservation as priorities for the islands' biodiversity.
records.referenceDate: Lakshadweep Administration Environment and Forest Department profile, updated 6 August 2025

records.name: Coconut and backyard horticulture
records.description: The Lakshadweep Agriculture Department prioritises coconut cultivation and organic household/backyard vegetable production. Its Nutri Garden scheme distributes vegetable and fruit planting material including tomato, brinjal, chilli, sapota, mango and guava.
records.referenceDate: Lakshadweep Administration Agriculture Department profile, updated 6 August 2025

records.name: Red-yellow, alluvial, laterite and medium-black soils
records.description: The Surguja District Administration identifies red and yellow soils, alluvial soils, laterite soils and medium-blue/black soils in northern Chhattisgarh. The cited profile is district-specific and should not be read as a statewide percentage distribution.
records.referenceDate: Surguja District Administration physical-resources profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Red, black, alluvial and lateritic soils
records.description: Telangana's Statistical Abstract 2021 identifies red soils (including chalkas and dubbas), shallow and deep black soils, alluvial soils and lateritic soils, with zone-wise variation across Northern, Central and Southern Telangana.
records.referenceDate: Telangana Statistical Abstract 2021

records.name: Alluvial, Shivalik, temperate black and inner-valley soils
records.description: Uttarakhand's State Action Plan on Climate Change describes deep alluvial soils in the Tarai and Doon, thin fragile soils in the Shivaliks, black soils in temperate zones and arid soils in inner valleys; NBSS&LUP texture classes include sandy loam, clay loam, fine silt and loamy skeletal soils.
records.referenceDate: Uttarakhand State Action Plan on Climate Change

records.name: Siwalik piedmont and Indo-Gangetic alluvial soils
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's 2025 Chandigarh report describes Siwalik formations at the north-eastern fringe, piedmont deposits of cobbles, pebbles and boulders, and the alluvial plain's clay, silt and sand deposits.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Chandigarh groundwater report, 2025

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Lateritic and black soils in Dadra and Nagar Haveli
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Dadra and Nagar Haveli district profile identifies lateritic soil, shallow black-cotton soil and deep black-cotton soil. This entry covers the Dadra and Nagar Haveli portion of the combined Union Territory.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board district profile, 2013

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Basalt, alluvial and coastal soils in Daman and Diu
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's 2023–24 Union Territory yearbook describes basalt basement, river alluvium and coastal deposits in Daman, and miliolite limestone and stabilised sand dunes in Diu. The profile distinguishes the two coastal districts from the DNH lateritic/black-soil terrain.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu Year Book 2023–24

records.name: Cold-desert Entisols and Inceptisols
records.description: ICAR-NBSS&LUP's Leh soil-resource mapping identifies Entisols and Inceptisols, with occasional Alfisols; mountain and glacier-derived terrain includes shallow skeletal Lithic Cryorthents, while valley soils range from sandy loam to loam and clay loam.
records.referenceDate: ICAR-NBSS&LUP Annual Report 2020, Leh soil-resource mapping

records.name: Shree Mahadev Temple, South Andaman
records.description: The South Andaman District Administration lists the Shree Mahadev Temple Committee as an official public institution associated with a place of worship in the district.
records.referenceDate: Official South Andaman district record accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Temples, gurdwaras, churches and mosques
records.description: Chandigarh Administration's social-infrastructure report records places of worship across the Union Territory, including temples, gurdwaras, churches and mosques. This is an institutional inventory rather than a claim that every listed site is an ancient monument.
records.referenceDate: Chandigarh Administration social-infrastructure report, 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Church of Our Lady of Piety, Daman
records.description: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Administration's tourism/heritage listing identifies the Church of Our Lady of Piety as a historic religious site in Daman.
records.referenceDate: Official UT/district heritage listing accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: St Paul's Church and Diu religious heritage
records.description: The Diu District Administration's official tourist-place directory records Diu Fort and historic churches, including St Paul's Church, as heritage attractions on Diu Island.
records.referenceDate: Official Diu district tourist-place directory accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Delhi's multi-faith heritage circuit
records.description: Delhi Tourism's faith itinerary documents major places of worship and religious heritage, including Jama Masjid, Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, Lotus Temple and other Hindu, Sikh, Muslim, Christian and Baháʼí sites.
records.referenceDate: Delhi Tourism faith itinerary accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ujra Mosque and Kavaratti religious heritage
records.description: The Lakshadweep Administration's Kavaratti island profile identifies Ujra Mosque among the island's heritage attractions and places of worship.
records.referenceDate: Lakshadweep Administration Kavaratti island profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Manakula Vinayagar Temple and historic churches
records.description: The Puducherry Planning Authority's official tourism and heritage material identifies Manakula Vinayagar Temple and the Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus among the Union Territory's prominent religious heritage sites.
records.referenceDate: Puducherry Planning Authority official profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Dudhni and Vanganga lakes
records.description: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli Administration identifies Dudhni Lake and Vanganga Lake among the Union Territory's major visitor water bodies; both are in the Dadra and Nagar Haveli district portion of the combined UT.
records.referenceDate: Official DNH district tourism profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Pangong Tso, Tso Moriri and Tso Kar
records.description: The Ladakh Administration's tourism directory identifies Pangong Tso, Tso Moriri and Tso Kar as major high-altitude lakes of the Union Territory.
records.referenceDate: Official Ladakh Administration tourism directory accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Kavaratti, Agatti and Bangaram lagoons
records.description: The Lakshadweep Administration's island profiles identify the shallow reef lagoons surrounding Kavaratti, Agatti and Bangaram as major marine water bodies and visitor features.
records.referenceDate: Official Lakshadweep Administration island profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Rani Gaidinliu and the Naga resistance to British rule
records.description: The Peren District Administration's disaster-management plan records Rani Gaidinliu's role in the Heraka movement and resistance to British rule in the Naga Hills, including her arrest in 1932.
records.referenceDate: Peren District Disaster Management Plan, Government of Nagaland

records.name: Battle of Aberdeen, Cellular Jail and the Azad Hind flag
records.description: South Andaman's official history records the 1859 Battle of Aberdeen and the islands' later role as a penal settlement for freedom fighters. Port Blair was also visited by Subhas Chandra Bose, who hoisted the Indian flag in December 1943.
records.referenceDate: Official South Andaman district history accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Liberation from Portuguese rule, 1954 and 1961
records.description: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli district history records liberation from Portuguese rule on 2 August 1954; Daman and Diu were integrated into India on 19 December 1961. These are anti-colonial liberation milestones for the combined Union Territory.
records.referenceDate: Official UT and district historical profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Delhi in the Revolt of 1857
records.description: Delhi Tourism's official history records the city as a major centre of the 1857 uprising, including the capture of the Red Fort and the fall of the Mughal court; the city remained a major site of later nationalist mobilisation.
records.referenceDate: Official Delhi Tourism history profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: 1931 popular movement and Quit Kashmir, 1946
records.description: Parliamentary and archival histories document the 1931 political agitation in Kashmir and Sheikh Abdullah's Quit Kashmir movement of 1946. These events form part of the modern political and anti-autocratic history of the former princely State.
records.referenceDate: Parliament of India biographical series and Nehru Archive, 1931–1946

records.name: No separate pre-independence city-level movement record
records.description: Chandigarh was planned after Independence and became a Union Territory in 1966. The current city therefore has no separate pre-1947 city-level freedom-movement chronology in the cited Chandigarh Administration history; events in the wider pre-1947 region are recorded under Punjab/Ambala.
records.referenceDate: Chandigarh Administration historical background accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: No separate anti-colonial movement record for present UT
records.description: The official Ladakh history describes the region's historical administration within the wider Jammu and Kashmir polity; it does not identify a distinct British-era anti-colonial movement episode for the present UT boundaries. This is a scope-limited attribution, not a claim that the region had no political resistance.
records.referenceDate: Official Ladakh Administration history profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: No distinct organised freedom-movement episode listed
records.description: The Lakshadweep Administration's official history documents British administration and the islands' later integration into the Indian Union, but does not identify a distinct organised anti-colonial movement episode for the islands. This statement is limited to the cited official history profile.
records.referenceDate: Official Lakshadweep Administration history profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Nicobari folk songs and community music
records.description: The Nicobar District Administration's culture-and-heritage profile documents traditional Nicobari folk songs, community performance and music as part of the islands' living cultural heritage.
records.referenceDate: Official Nicobar District culture and heritage profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Punjabi folk music shared across the Chandigarh region
records.description: Chandigarh's cultural life is closely connected with the Punjabi cultural region. Punjab Government cultural material documents Bhangra and Giddha folk-music and performance traditions; this is a shared regional tradition, not a music form originating solely in the Union Territory.
records.referenceDate: Punjab Government cultural profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Warli folk songs, Tarpa and tribal music
records.description: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli Administration's cultural profile documents Warli folk songs, the Tarpa instrument and community music-and-dance traditions, including Dhol, Tur and Thali performances.
records.referenceDate: Official Dadra and Nagar Haveli cultural profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Sufi qawwali and the Nizamuddin musical tradition
records.description: Delhi Tourism's heritage and spiritual itineraries identify Nizamuddin Auliya's dargah as a major Sufi centre; the city's qawwali and devotional music traditions are closely associated with the shrine and the legacy of Amir Khusrau.
records.referenceDate: Official Delhi Tourism spiritual itinerary accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Sufiana Mausiqi, Chakri and Rouf traditions
records.description: The Jammu and Kashmir Tourism Development Corporation documents Sufiana Mausiqi, Chakri and Rouf among the region's established music and performance traditions.
records.referenceDate: Jammu and Kashmir Tourism Development Corporation cultural profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ladakhi folk songs and ceremonial music
records.description: The Ladakh Administration's cultural-event report documents traditional forms including Lharna, Shondol, Jabro and Junglu, alongside ceremonial and monastery-linked music traditions.
records.referenceDate: Official Ladakh Administration cultural report accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Lava, Kolkali, Parichakali and Mappila songs
records.description: The Lakshadweep Administration's culture-and-heritage profile documents Lava, Kolkali and Parichakali performances, as well as Mappila song traditions, as part of the islands' cultural life.
records.referenceDate: Official Lakshadweep Administration culture and heritage profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Tamil folk and Carnatic music traditions
records.description: The Puducherry Department of Art and Culture documents the Union Territory's Tamil folk and classical music traditions, alongside the French-influenced cultural history of Puducherry town.
records.referenceDate: Puducherry Department of Art and Culture profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Rani Gaidinliu
records.description: The Peren District Administration records Rani Gaidinliu as a central figure in the Heraka movement and the Naga resistance to British rule; her legacy is preserved in the district's historical profile.
records.referenceDate: Peren District Disaster Management Plan, Government of Nagaland

records.name: Subhas Chandra Bose and Veer Savarkar
records.description: South Andaman's official history records Subhas Chandra Bose's 1943 visit to Port Blair and the islands' role in the imprisonment of freedom fighters, including Veer Savarkar at Cellular Jail.
records.referenceDate: Official South Andaman district history accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret
records.description: Chandigarh Administration identifies Le Corbusier as the lead architect of the city's master plan from 1951 and records Pierre Jeanneret's role as chief architect and town-planning adviser.
records.referenceDate: Official Chandigarh Administration historical background accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: No named personality in the cited district-history profiles
records.description: The cited official DNH and Diu district history profiles document the region's dynasties, Portuguese period and liberation milestones but do not identify a named historical personality in the sections used for this catalogue. This is a source-scope note, not a claim that the Union Territory had no notable people.
records.referenceDate: Official DNH and Diu district history profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Bahadur Shah Zafar and Mirza Ghalib
records.description: Delhi Tourism's history and heritage profiles document Bahadur Shah Zafar's association with the 1857 uprising and Mirza Ghalib's literary life in the city, including Ghalib Ki Haveli.
records.referenceDate: Official Delhi Tourism heritage profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah
records.description: The Parliament of India's biographical series documents Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah's role in the political history of Jammu and Kashmir, including the 1931 agitation and the Quit Kashmir movement.
records.referenceDate: Parliament of India biographical series

records.name: Kushok Bakula Rinpoche
records.description: The Ladakh Administration's 2026 tribute describes Kushok Bakula Rinpoche as a spiritual master, social reformer, diplomat and statesman whose work shaped modern Ladakh and strengthened India–Mongolia cultural relations.
records.referenceDate: Ladakh Administration, 8 May 2026

records.name: St. Ubaidullah
records.description: The Lakshadweep Administration's official history identifies St. Ubaidullah as a central figure in the early spread of Islam in the islands and records his burial at Andrott as a revered historical and religious site.
records.referenceDate: Official Lakshadweep Administration history profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Cashew, coconut and fruit horticulture
records.description: Goa's Directorate of Agriculture administers agriculture and horticulture across the State. The Union Ministry of Agriculture's 2025–26 estimate records 17.87 thousand tonnes of cashew production in Goa, a key horticultural crop; the State also promotes coconut, mango and other plantation/fruit crops.
records.referenceDate: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, 21 July 2026

records.name: Coconut, arecanut, tropical fruit and spice crops
records.description: ICAR's 2025 Kharif agro-advisory for the islands identifies coconut and arecanut plantations, banana, mango, sapota, papaya, pineapple and citrus fruits, together with pepper, cinnamon, turmeric and ginger.
records.referenceDate: ICAR Kharif Agro-Advisories for Farmers, 2025

records.name: Urban gardens, green belts and park horticulture
records.description: Chandigarh Municipal Corporation's Horticulture and Electrical Wing maintains neighbourhood parks, gardens, green belts and landscaping; this is an urban-horticulture profile rather than a commercial fruit-crop estimate.
records.referenceDate: Chandigarh Municipal Corporation RTI disclosure, updated 28 November 2024

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Chikoo and fruit horticulture in Daman and DNH
records.description: The UT Agriculture Department administers agriculture, soil conservation and horticulture. Its 2026 notices include the auction of chikoo fruit from Daman, documenting the region's sapota orchards and fruit-horticulture activity.
records.referenceDate: UT Agriculture Department notices, August 2026

records.name: Urban horticulture, parks and green belts
records.description: Delhi's Green Action Plan documents the work of the Environment Department Horticulture Unit and the Delhi Parks and Gardens Society in planting and maintaining the Ridge, Yamuna floodplain, parks, nurseries and city green cover.
records.referenceDate: Government of NCT of Delhi — Green Action Plan, 2026

records.name: Apricot, apple, walnut and sea-buckthorn cultivation
records.description: The Ladakh Horticulture Department reports apricot and apple cultivation, walnut and other dry fruits, and expansion of fruit orchards. Its official statistics report 2,612 hectares of apricot and 866 hectares of apple cultivation, with sea-buckthorn development programmes.
records.referenceDate: Ladakh Horticulture Department profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Coconut and backyard fruit and vegetable gardens
records.description: The Lakshadweep Agriculture Department's Nutri Garden scheme supports household and backyard horticulture with tomato, brinjal, chilli, sapota, mango and guava seedlings, alongside the Coconut Development Programme.
records.referenceDate: Lakshadweep Agriculture Department profile, updated 6 August 2025

records.name: Coconut, banana and diversified fruit and vegetable crops
records.description: Puducherry's Integrated Horticulture Development Programme supports fruit and vegetable seed kits, banana and coconut seedlings and backyard gardens. The 2023–24 Statistical Report records 1,835 hectares under coconut and 20.191 million nuts produced.
records.referenceDate: Puducherry Gazette, 30 October 2023; Statistical Report 2023–24

records.name: Minor mineral production; no major mineral production reported
records.description: The Indian Bureau of Mines' 2022 Union Territories review reports no major mineral production from Andaman and Nicobar Islands in 2021–22, while minor-mineral production was reported. The same review lists mineral-based cement and sponge-iron industries; it does not provide a complete inventory of minor mineral occurrences.
records.referenceDate: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 — Union Territories, June 2024

records.name: No major or minor mineral production reported
records.description: The Indian Bureau of Mines' 2022 Union Territories review reports no production of major or minor minerals from Chandigarh during 2021–22. This is a production-status statement and does not assert that every geological material is absent.
records.referenceDate: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 — Union Territories, June 2024

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Limestone resources in Daman and Diu; no reported production in 2021–22
records.description: The Indian Bureau of Mines' 2022 Union Territories review reports no major or minor mineral production from Dadra and Nagar Haveli or Daman and Diu in 2021–22. It separately records about 12.867 million tonnes of limestone resources for Daman and Diu and documents mineral-based industries in Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
records.referenceDate: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 — Union Territories, June 2024

records.name: Kaolin, fireclay and quartz-silica occurrences
records.description: The Indian Bureau of Mines' Delhi State Review records kaolin deposits west of Qutub Minar at Mehrauli, Masoodpur, Kusumpur and Mahipalpur, along with fireclay and Badarpur sand/quartzite occurrences. The review also reports measured and inferred clay resources.
records.referenceDate: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 — Delhi, July 2024

records.name: Borax, sapphire, sulphur, graphite, marble, gypsum and limestone
records.description: The Indian Bureau of Mines' Jammu and Kashmir State Review identifies borax, sapphire and native sulphur resources, along with graphite, marble, gypsum, coal, limestone, magnesite, bauxite, china clay and other minerals. It records coal and limestone as principal producing minerals in 2021–22.
records.referenceDate: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 — Jammu and Kashmir, July 2024

records.name: Borax, limestone and magnesite in the Leh region
records.description: The Indian Bureau of Mines' 2022 review of the former Jammu and Kashmir State specifically records borax in Leh district and limestone and magnesite occurrences in Leh. The report predates the current UT's separate statistical series, so the cited district-level mineral information is retained with that boundary caveat.
records.referenceDate: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 — Jammu and Kashmir, July 2024; Leh district data

records.name: No major or minor mineral production reported
records.description: The Indian Bureau of Mines' 2022 Union Territories review reports no production of major or minor minerals from Lakshadweep during 2021–22. This is limited to the review's production reporting and is not a geological claim that no mineral-bearing material exists.
records.referenceDate: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 — Union Territories, June 2024

records.name: Limestone and lignite resources; no reported production in 2021–22
records.description: The Indian Bureau of Mines' 2022 Union Territories review reports no major or minor mineral production in Puducherry during 2021–22, but records limestone resources and 416.61 million tonnes of lignite resources in the Bahour and western Bahour area of the Neyveli Lignite Field.
records.referenceDate: Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 — Union Territories, June 2024

records.name: Ranganadi Reservoir
records.description: NEEPCO's Ranganadi Hydro Electric Project forms a reservoir behind the concrete/rock-fill dam on the Ranganadi River. The project data sheet records 5.70 million cubic metres of live storage; the scheme is operated by NEEPCO.
records.referenceDate: NEEPCO Ranganadi Hydro Electric Project salient-features filing, 2024

records.name: Kaushalya Dam Reservoir
records.description: The Ministry of Jal Shakti's December 2025 Lok Sabha reply records Kaushalya Dam in Haryana with original gross storage of 13.68 MCM and current gross storage of 12.42 MCM, based on recent survey data.
records.referenceDate: Ministry of Jal Shakti Lok Sabha reply, 4 December 2025

records.name: Khuga Reservoir
records.description: The Central Water and Power Research Station's 2020–21 annual report records a bathymetric survey of Khuga Reservoir. The multipurpose dam on the Khuga River supplies drinking water and irrigation to Churachandpur and surrounding areas.
records.referenceDate: CWPRS Annual Report 2020–21

records.name: Teesta-V Reservoir
records.description: NHPC's Teesta-V project document records a gross reservoir storage of 13.52 MCM at full reservoir level. Sikkim's September 2026 district-administration release reports that the dam site was restored and the project recommissioned in July 2026 following the 2023 GLOF damage.
records.referenceDate: NHPC Teesta-V project document; Sikkim Government release, September 2026

records.name: Kalpong Dam Reservoir
records.description: The North and Middle Andaman District Administration identifies Kalpong as the islands' largest dam, built across the Kalpong River at Nabagram, Diglipur. The district profile records a storage capacity of 15.27 million cubic metres and a reservoir area of about 1.84 square kilometres.
records.referenceDate: Official North and Middle Andaman district profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Sukhna Lake Reservoir
records.description: Chandigarh Administration describes Sukhna Lake as an artificial lake created in 1958 by damming the seasonal Sukhna Choe. The lake is a managed rain-fed storage water body at the Shivalik foothills.
records.referenceDate: Chandigarh Administration physical-setting profile

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Madhuban Dam Reservoir
records.description: The Central Water Commission records the Madhuban Dam/Damanganga Reservoir project as an inter-State agreement involving Gujarat and the former Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The reservoir is on the Damanganga system and serves the adjoining region.
records.referenceDate: Central Water Commission legal-institutional compendium; agreement dated 29 September 1992

records.name: Delhi Jal Board service reservoirs
records.description: Delhi Jal Board's official work-allocation disclosure lists service reservoirs at Hindu Rao, Jeet Garh, Flag Staff, Jhandewalan, Shadipur, Janta Park, Talkatora, Hasanpur, Ridge Road and Rajinder Nagar. These are urban water-supply storage reservoirs rather than dam reservoirs.
records.referenceDate: Delhi Jal Board public-information disclosure accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Salal Reservoir
records.description: NHPC's 2026 Salal Power Station document describes the reservoir formed by the rock-fill and concrete dams on the Chenab. It records gross storage of 284.08 MCM at commissioning and a current capacity of 13.95 MCM at full pond level in the 2024 survey, reflecting substantial sedimentation.
records.referenceDate: NHPC Salal Power Station reservoir survey/tender document, 2026

records.name: Nimoo-Bazgo hydroelectric pondage
records.description: NHPC describes Nimoo-Bazgo as a run-of-river hydroelectric scheme on the Indus at Alchi, Leh, with a small pondage behind its concrete gravity dam. This is a small operational pondage, not a large seasonal storage reservoir.
records.referenceDate: NHPC Nimoo-Bazgo project profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: No specified dam reservoir listed
records.description: The National Register of Specified Dams 2025 does not list a specified dam for Lakshadweep. This is limited to dams meeting the Dam Safety Act's specified-dam thresholds; it does not exclude small ponds, rainwater-storage structures or household cisterns.
records.referenceDate: National Register of Specified Dams 2025, April 2025

records.name: Bahour Irrigation Tank
records.description: Puducherry's official water-body inventory records Bahour Tank at 494.4 hectares, owned by the Public Works Department and used for irrigation of nearby agricultural fields. It is a traditional irrigation-storage tank, not a large dam reservoir.
records.referenceDate: Puducherry water-body inventory, 2024

records.name: Steel, aluminium, cement, power and food processing
records.description: Chhattisgarh's Industries Department identifies steel, aluminium, cement, thermal power and mineral-based manufacturing as core sectors. The State also promotes agro and food processing, IT/ITeS, electronics, textiles, automotive, engineering goods, defence and logistics.
records.referenceDate: Government of Chhattisgarh — Industrial Scenario and Industrial Development Policy 2024–30

records.name: Coconut and marine food processing, coir, handicrafts and shipping
records.description: The Andaman and Nicobar Directorate of Industries identifies sustainable MSMEs, eco-tourism, coconut and marine-based food processing, handicrafts, coir, wooden/cane products, fisheries, shipping and port-management services as priority opportunities. Its district ODOP products include coconut-based products and marine products.
records.referenceDate: Andaman and Nicobar Administration — Directorate of Industries, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: MSMEs, IT/ITeS, startups and light manufacturing
records.description: Chandigarh's Department of Industries supports MSMEs, startups and entrepreneurship, while the Chandigarh Industrial Policy and Master Plan identify IT/ITeS, knowledge-based services, light manufacturing and the Phase I/II industrial areas and IT Park as the UT's industrial base.
records.referenceDate: Chandigarh Administration Department of Industries profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Textiles, plastics, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and food processing
records.description: The UT District Industries Centre supports industrial estates and MSMEs in Daman and DNH. Official industrial-unit disclosures identify textile printing, plastics and polymers, pharmaceuticals, packaging, glass and chemical manufacturing, alongside food-processing and cold-chain projects.
records.referenceDate: UT District Industries Centre and official industrial-unit disclosures accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Engineering, electronics, IT, pharmaceuticals and small manufacturing
records.description: The Government of NCT Delhi identifies the city as a major commercial and small-industries centre, with manufacturing in electrical and light-engineering machinery, automobile parts, sports goods, bicycles, PVC goods, footwear, textiles, fertilizers, medicines, hosiery, leather and software. Its industrial policy promotes electronics, telecommunications, software and IT-enabled services.
records.referenceDate: Government of NCT Delhi — About Us, Industry profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Food processing, handicrafts, tourism and MSME manufacturing
records.description: Jammu and Kashmir's Economic Survey 2025–26 identifies agriculture, food processing, handicrafts, tourism and education as key industrial focus areas. MSMEs account for nearly 60% of industrial investment and about 90% of industrial employment; the UT's industrial policy and Central Sector Scheme support manufacturing and services expansion.
records.referenceDate: Jammu and Kashmir Economic Survey 2025–26, Industries and Commerce chapter

records.name: Pashmina processing, handicrafts, food processing and sustainable MSMEs
records.description: Ladakh's Industries and Commerce Department administers the Sustainable Industrial Policy 2022–27 and industrial land-allotment policy. The UT is developing pashmina dehairing and processing facilities in Leh, alongside handicrafts, local-resource-based micro-enterprises and food processing.
records.referenceDate: Ladakh Administration Industries and Commerce Department profile, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Coir, coconut processing, tuna and marine products
records.description: The Lakshadweep Industries Department identifies coir production, coconut-based industries, handicrafts and eco-friendly MSMEs as priority sectors. The Fisheries Department documents tuna as the principal fishery resource, pole-and-line fishing, tuna processing at Minicoy and value-added marine products.
records.referenceDate: Lakshadweep Administration Industries Department profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Food, textiles, chemicals, plastics, engineering and pharmaceuticals
records.description: Puducherry's official Industrial Profile records 9,307 permanently registered industrial units as of 31 January 2019, with major groups in food products, cotton and wool, wood, paper and printing, leather/rubber/plastics, chemicals, non-metallic minerals, metal products and machinery. The Department's priority sectors include electronics, IT, auto components, agro/food processing, marine products, pharmaceuticals and textiles.
records.referenceDate: Government of Puducherry — Industries and Commerce Department, Industrial Profile
