records.name: Chorla Ghat and Bhagaza Ghat
records.description: The National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organisation's State Atlas of Goa identifies two Western Ghats outcrops in the State: Chorla Ghat in the north and Bhagaza Ghat in the east. The North Goa District Disaster Management Plan also records the Sanquelim–Chorla Ghat road at the Karnataka boundary. These are named Western Ghats crossings rather than high Himalayan passes.
records.referenceDate: NATMO State Atlas of Goa; 2020

records.name: Palakkad Gap (Palghat Gap)
records.description: Kerala Tourism identifies the 30–40 km-wide Palakkad Gap as the lowest pass through the Western Ghats and a natural corridor between Kerala and Tamil Nadu. It is a major geographic pass connecting the east and west sides of the southern peninsula.
records.referenceDate: Kerala Tourism destination profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Bhor, Malshej, Tamhini, Amboli, Varandha, Kasara, Kumbharli, Kashedi and Amba Ghats
records.description: The Maharashtra Tourism Department's 2025 pocket guide identifies these named Western Ghats crossings and describes the State's ghats as mountain passes. The listed routes connect the Konkan coast with the Deccan plateau and adjoining uplands.
records.referenceDate: Maharashtra Tourism pocket guide, 2025

records.name: Talakona Waterfall
records.description: The Tirupati District Administration identifies Talakona as the highest waterfall in Andhra Pradesh, located within Sri Venkateswara National Park, with a reported 270-foot fall.
records.referenceDate: Official Tirupati District Administration forest tourism profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Sirki Waterfall, Chumi Gyatse and Matu Waterfall
records.description: Arunachal Tourism lists Sirki Waterfall near Pasighat and Chumi Gyatse's 108 cascades near Tawang; its 2025 calendar also profiles Matu Waterfall near Anini. These examples demonstrate waterfall features across the State's eastern and western districts.
records.referenceDate: Arunachal Tourism official destination profiles and 2025 calendar

records.name: Kakolat, Telhar Kund, Karakatgarh, Tutla Bhawani, Manjhar Kund and Dhuan Kund
records.description: Bihar Tourism's official destination catalogue lists waterfalls in Nawada and Kaimur/Rohtas, including Kakolat, Telhar Kund, Karakatgarh, Tutla Bhawani, Manjhar Kund and Dhuan Kund.
records.referenceDate: Bihar Tourism official Eco Circuit and district destination profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Sadu Chiru Waterfall
records.description: The Government of Manipur's tourism policy identifies Sadu Chiru Waterfall in Sadar Hills, describing three cascades near Imphal as a tourist attraction.
records.referenceDate: Government of Manipur Tourism Policy; Tamenglong District Disaster Management Plan

records.name: Vantawng Khawhthla, Tuirihiau, Tuisen Tlabung and Tuirivang Falls
records.description: The Mizoram Government's protocol and Serchhip district profiles document Vantawng Khawhthla, Tuirihiau, Tuisen Tlabung and Tuirivang waterfalls, including Vantawng's approximately 750-foot cascade.
records.referenceDate: Government of Mizoram places-of-interest profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Sosu Rochu and Suteplenden Waterfalls; Dzukou Waterfall
records.description: Nagaland's Directorate of Tourism statistical handbook lists Sosu Rochu and Suteplenden waterfalls among the State's tourist spots. The State Tourism Policy also identifies Dzukou Waterfall and other seasonal falls as monsoon attractions.
records.referenceDate: Nagaland Statistical Handbook 2021, Directorate of Tourism; Nagaland Tourism Policy

records.name: Kuntala, Bogatha, Pochera and Gayatri Waterfalls
records.description: Telangana Tourism documents Kuntala as the State's tallest waterfall and profiles Bogatha and Pochera. The Adilabad district tourism profile also identifies Gayatri Falls on the Kadam River.
records.referenceDate: Telangana Tourism official nature and district profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Baramura Waterfall
records.description: The Tripura Biodiversity Board's technical report documents Baramura Waterfall as a perennial stream-fed cascade in the Baramura Reserve Forest, near Teliamura in Khowai district. The report records its approximate height and location, making it a documented physical-geography feature.
records.referenceDate: Tripura Biodiversity Board technical report, 2016

records.name: Ananthagiri Ghats and the Araku Ghat Road
records.description: The Visakhapatnam District Administration describes the Araku Valley approach as a winding ghat road through the Ananthagiri Hills, with the Ananthagiri ghats forming the mountain crossing on the Eastern Ghats route. This is a regional ghat-road pass rather than a high-altitude Himalayan pass.
records.referenceDate: Official Visakhapatnam District geography profile

records.name: Charmadi Ghat and Shiradi Ghat
records.description: The Geological Survey of India documents landslide-susceptibility mapping along the Charmadi Ghat corridor on NH-73 and Shiradi Ghat on NH-75. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways also identifies the Charmadi Ghat stretch as a mountainous road corridor linking the coast and Malnad region.
records.referenceDate: Geological Survey of India, Field Season 2024–25

records.name: Palakkad Gap (eastern gateway through the Western Ghats)
records.description: Kerala Tourism describes the Palakkad Gap as the lowest pass through the Western Ghats and a natural corridor between Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The gap opens into the Coimbatore region on the Tamil Nadu side and has historically connected the east and west coasts.
records.referenceDate: Kerala Tourism destination profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Galikonda Peak
records.description: The Polavaram District Administration identifies Galikonda, in the Eastern Ghats near Araku, as one of Andhra Pradesh's highest peaks at approximately 1,500 metres. The source describes it as among the State's highest rather than asserting an exclusive state record.
records.referenceDate: Official Polavaram District Administration geography profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Someshwar Range high point
records.description: The Government of India's Incredible India state profile identifies the Someshwar Range in West Champaran, at approximately 875–880 metres, as Bihar's highest mountain peak.
records.referenceDate: Incredible India, Government of India

records.name: Gaurlata Peak, Dipadih
records.description: The Balrampur-Ramanujganj District Administration identifies Gaurlata at Dipadih as the highest peak of Chhattisgarh and records it among the district's defining geographical features.
records.referenceDate: Official Balrampur-Ramanujganj District Administration profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Girnar Peak
records.description: The Gujarat Water Resources Department's geographical profile identifies Girnar as the most prominent hill range in Saurashtra and records its highest peak at approximately 1,117 metres above mean sea level.
records.referenceDate: Government of Gujarat, Water Resources Department Annual Administrative Report 2009–10

records.name: Dhupgarh Peak, Satpura Range
records.description: The Government of India's India Cine Hub profile identifies Dhupgarh, in the Satpura Range near Pachmarhi, as the highest point in Madhya Pradesh at approximately 1,350 metres.
records.referenceDate: India Cine Hub, Government of India profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Shillong Peak
records.description: The Meghalaya Government's investment portal describes Shillong Peak at approximately 6,446 feet as the State's highest peak and identifies it as a tourism destination.
records.referenceDate: Government of Meghalaya, Tourism Department project profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Phawngpui Tlang (Blue Mountain)
records.description: The Mizoram Environment, Forests and Climate Change Department identifies the peak within Phawngpui National Park as the highest point in the State at 2,157 metres above mean sea level.
records.referenceDate: Official Mizoram Forest Department profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Mount Saramati
records.description: The Kiphire District Administration's district-level land-use report identifies Mount Saramati at approximately 3,841 metres as Nagaland's highest peak.
records.referenceDate: Kiphire District Administration / Nagaland district SLUP report

records.name: Deomali Peak, Eastern Ghats
records.description: The Koraput District Administration and Odisha Tourism identify Deomali at approximately 1,672 metres as the highest peak in Odisha, located in the Eastern Ghats.
records.referenceDate: Official Koraput District Administration and Odisha Tourism profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Betlingchhip Peak, Jampui Hills
records.description: The National Portal of India identifies Betlingchhip as the highest point in Tripura, in the Jampui Hills, at approximately 3,000 feet.
records.referenceDate: National Portal of India, Government of India, accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Saddle Peak, North Andaman
records.description: NITI Aayog's island physiography profile identifies Saddle Peak at 732 metres as the highest point in the Andaman group, located on North Andaman Island.
records.referenceDate: NITI Aayog island physiography profile

records.name: Chota Nagpur Plateau (southern Bihar historical region)
records.description: The Planning Commission's archived Bihar Government Second Five-Year Plan identifies three natural divisions in the then Bihar State: North Bihar Plains, South Bihar Plains and the Chota Nagpur Plateau. Present-day Bihar retains the northern part of the historical plateau region; the entry is a historical-physiographic attribution, not a claim that the entire Chota Nagpur Plateau lies within present Bihar.
records.referenceDate: Planning Commission / Government of Bihar, Draft Second Five-Year Plan, 1955

records.name: Bastar Plateau and Chhattisgarh Plain
records.description: The Durg District Administration's state topography profile distinguishes the Bastar Plateau in the south, the Northern Hilly Region and the Plains of Chhattisgarh. The Bastar Plateau includes Bastar, Dantewada, Bijapur and Narayanpur districts and part of Kanker.
records.referenceDate: Official Durg District Administration geography profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Central Upland Plateau
records.description: The National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organisation's State Atlas of Goa identifies the Central Upland Plateau as a distinct physiographic unit between the Western Ghats and the western coastal plains, with dissected lateritic uplands and river valleys.
records.referenceDate: National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organisation, State Atlas of Goa

records.name: Saurashtra Plateau and Kachchh Upland
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Gujarat groundwater assessment divides the State into physiographic zones and identifies the uplands of Saurashtra and Kachchh as plateau regions, with Mount Girnar rising from the Saurashtra upland.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Ground Water Resources Assessment 2022 — Gujarat

records.name: Karewa elevated tablelands of the Kashmir Valley
records.description: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons' National Data Repository describes Karewa as elevated table-land: unconsolidated to semi-consolidated sand, clay and conglomerate sediments forming terraces, plateaus and mounds around the Kashmir Basin.
records.referenceDate: Directorate General of Hydrocarbons, National Data Repository — Karewa Basin profile

records.name: Ladakh High-Altitude Plateau and Changthang Plateau
records.description: The Ladakh Disaster Management Authority's Leh district profile describes Ladakh as India's highest-altitude plateau region, with elevations of approximately 2,900–5,900 metres. The high plateau landscape includes the Changthang region and adjoining trans-Himalayan tablelands.
records.referenceDate: Ladakh Disaster Management Authority — Leh District Profile

records.name: Dalpat Sagar and Ganga Munda Lakes, Jagdalpur
records.description: The Government of India's Incredible India tourism itinerary identifies Dalpat Sagar as the largest artificial lake in Chhattisgarh and records Ganga Munda as another lake within Jagdalpur town.
records.referenceDate: Government of India tourism profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Damdama Lake, Gurugram district
records.description: The Gurugram District Administration identifies Damdama Lake near Sohna as a major scenic water body and tourist destination; Haryana Tourism operates the adjoining Saras Tourist Complex.
records.referenceDate: Official Gurugram District Administration profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Karanji Lake, Kukkarahalli Lake and Lingambudhi Lake, Mysuru
records.description: The Ministry of Tourism's Swadesh Darshan 2.0 destination master plan for Mysuru documents Karanji, Kukkarahalli and Lingambudhi lakes, including their location, ecological significance and restoration/protection status.
records.referenceDate: Ministry of Tourism, Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Mysuru Destination Master Plan

records.name: Bhojtal (Upper Lake) and Lower Lake, Bhopal
records.description: The Bhopal Development Plan and Town and Country Planning Department documents Bhojtal (Upper Lake), its catchment and the Lower Lake, recording their origin, ecological zones and statutory protection measures.
records.referenceDate: Government of Madhya Pradesh, Bhopal Development Plan 2031

records.name: Umiam Lake (Barapani)
records.description: The Ri Bhoi District Administration records Umiam Lake as a reservoir created by damming the Umiam River in the early 1960s and documents its water-based recreation and surrounding landscape.
records.referenceDate: Official Ri Bhoi District Administration profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Palak Dil, Tam Dil, Rung Dil and Rengdil
records.description: The Mizoram Directorate of Information and Public Relations identifies Palak Dil, Tam Dil, Rung Dil and Rengdil among the State's principal lakes and records Palak Dil's approximate 30-hectare area and Tam Dil's natural-lake status.
records.referenceDate: Official Mizoram Directorate of Information and Public Relations geography profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Shilloi Lake, Phek district
records.description: The Nagaland State Pollution Control Board's EIACP newsletter identifies Shilloi as the State's largest natural lake, located in Phek district at approximately 983 metres elevation. The Nagaland State Biodiversity Board also features Shilloi in its biodiversity profile.
records.referenceDate: Nagaland EIACP Newsletter, January–March 2025

records.name: Tsomgo, Gurudongmar, Chho Lhamo and Khecheopalri Lakes
records.description: The Government of Sikkim's Tourism and Civil Aviation Department lists Tsomgo, Gurudongmar, Chho Lhamo and Khecheopalri among the State's principal mountain lakes and documents their locations and cultural significance.
records.referenceDate: Government of Sikkim Tourism and Civil Aviation Department profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ooty Lake, Kodaikanal Lake, Pykara, Avalanche and Emerald Lakes
records.description: The Tamil Nadu Wetlands Authority's wetland brief for Kodaikanal Lake and the Ministry of Tourism's Nilgiris Destination Master Plan document major lakes and reservoirs including Ooty, Kodaikanal, Pykara, Avalanche and Emerald.
records.referenceDate: Ministry of Tourism, Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Nilgiris Destination Master Plan; Tamil Nadu Wetlands Authority

records.name: Hussain Sagar Lake, Hyderabad
records.description: The Hyderabad District Administration documents Hussain Sagar as an artificial lake constructed in 1562 on a tributary of the Musi River. It connects Hyderabad and Secunderabad and remains a major urban water body and recreation site.
records.referenceDate: Official Hyderabad District Administration profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ramgarh Tal, Gorakhpur
records.description: The National Institute of Disaster Management's wetland site profile identifies Ramgarh Tal as a perennial freshwater lake connected to the Rapti River and records its area, ecological condition and Ramsar-site importance.
records.referenceDate: National Institute of Disaster Management wetland site profile, 2021

records.name: Sumendu Lake (Mirik Lake)
records.description: West Bengal Tourism identifies Sumendu Lake, also called Mirik Lake, as the central attraction of Mirik in Darjeeling district and documents its setting, approximate length and recreational uses.
records.referenceDate: West Bengal Tourism official destination profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Gandhi Park Lake, Sri Vijaya Puram
records.description: The Andaman and Nicobar Administration's 2024 Bird Watching Gazetteer identifies a lake within Gandhi Park in Sri Vijaya Puram and maps it as part of the South Andaman birding trail.
records.referenceDate: Andaman and Nicobar Administration Extraordinary Gazette, 2 August 2024

records.name: Sukhna Lake
records.description: Chandigarh Tourism documents Sukhna Lake as a 3-square-kilometre rain-fed lake created in 1958 by damming Sukhna Choe, and identifies it as a National Wetland.
records.referenceDate: Chandigarh Administration wetland brief, 2024

records.regionName: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
records.name: Vanganga Lake Garden and Dudhni Lake
records.description: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Administration documents Vanganga Lake Garden as a 7.58-hectare lake and Incredible India describes Dudhni Lake as the Madhuban Dam reservoir near Silvassa.
records.referenceDate: Official UT Administration and Incredible India destination profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Sanjay Lake, East Delhi
records.description: Delhi Tourism and the Delhi Development Authority identify Sanjay Lake in Trilokpuri as a 17-hectare artificial lake developed by back-flow from the Yamuna and Hindon channels, with a surrounding green belt and public recreation facilities.
records.referenceDate: Delhi Tourism and Delhi Development Authority profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Ousteri (Oussudu) Lake
records.description: The Ministry of Tourism's Puducherry Destination Master Plan identifies Ousteri Lake as an 800-hectare wetland shared by Puducherry and Tamil Nadu, with approximately 390 hectares in Puducherry. The lake is an important wetland and bird habitat.
records.referenceDate: Ministry of Tourism, Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Puducherry Destination Master Plan

records.name: No natural lakes; freshwater ponds and groundwater lenses instead
records.description: The Lakshadweep Administration's action plan filed before the National Green Tribunal states that lakes, ponds and wetlands in the conventional mainland sense do not exist in the UT, while noting that small freshwater ponds do occur and have been renovated. The islands' principal water features are coral lagoons, which are recorded separately under coastal and marine geography.
records.referenceDate: Lakshadweep Administration action plan, 2019

records.name: White Surf and Whisper Wave Waterfalls, Little Andaman
records.description: The Andaman and Nicobar Administration's official tourism portal describes Little Andaman as a waterfall destination and lists White Surf and Whisper Wave as natural waterfalls surrounded by tropical rainforest.
records.referenceDate: Official Andaman and Nicobar Tourism portal accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Aharbal Falls, Kulgam district
records.description: The Jammu and Kashmir Tourism Development Corporation describes Aharbal Falls on the Veshu River in the Pir Panjal range, where the river drops through a narrow granite gorge in two cascades.
records.referenceDate: Jammu and Kashmir Tourism Development Corporation destination profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Rajdari, Devdari, Chandraprabha, Lakhaniya Dari and Vindham Falls
records.description: The Uttar Pradesh Eco-Tourism Development Board lists Rajdari, Devdari and Chandraprabha waterfalls in Chandauli, and Lakhaniya Dari, Chuna Dari and Vindham Falls in Mirzapur among the State's natural attractions.
records.referenceDate: UP Eco-Tourism Development Board official site accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Changey Waterfall, Kalimpong district
records.description: West Bengal Tourism documents Changey Waterfall near Lava in Kalimpong district as a forested hillside waterfall with an approximately 150-foot cascade.
records.referenceDate: West Bengal Tourism official destination profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Chhattisgarh Plain and Indravati River plains
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board divides Chhattisgarh into the Bastar Plateau, central Chhattisgarh Plain and northern hills. It describes the central plain as a gently undulating structural plain across the Mahanadi basin and records lower river plains along the Indravati and Shabari.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board geomorphology report, 2022

records.name: Kangra Valley and lower foothill plains
records.description: The Himachal Pradesh State Agricultural Marketing Board's Kangra district profile documents the Kangra Valley, lower foothill plains around Nurpur, Indora and Fatehpur, and the Beas Basin as distinct physiographic and agricultural zones.
records.referenceDate: Official Himachal Pradesh Agricultural Marketing Board district profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Narmada Valley lowlands
records.description: The Khandwa District Administration identifies the Narmada Valley as one of the district's two major natural divisions, distinct from the Satpura ranges. The valley floor forms a lowland corridor across the western-central part of Madhya Pradesh.
records.referenceDate: Official Khandwa District Administration profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Imphal Valley (central alluvial plain)
records.description: The Government of Manipur describes the State as two physiographic regions: rugged outer hills and the inner flat plain. The Imphal Valley is an approximately 700-square-mile oval-shaped basin surrounded by mountains and filled with fluvio-lacustrine and alluvial sediments.
records.referenceDate: Official Manipur Government State Profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Dimapur alluvial plains
records.description: The Nagaland State Disaster Management Authority's State Disaster Management Plan describes a large part of Dimapur district as plains, with Dimapur town situated on a flat to gently undulating alluvial tract at an average elevation of approximately 260 metres.
records.referenceDate: Nagaland State Disaster Management Plan, 2019

records.name: Terai and Bhabar plains
records.description: The Uttarakhand Biodiversity Board identifies the Terai and Bhabar as distinct lowland physiographic zones along the Shiwalik foothills, with the Terai extending across the lower parts of Nainital district and adjoining river plains.
records.referenceDate: Uttarakhand Biodiversity Board State profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Jammu plains, Kandi belt and Kashmir Valley floor
records.description: NITI Aayog's 2026 Jammu and Kashmir horticulture roadmap describes the UT's physiography as mountainous and semi-mountainous plains (Kandi belt), Siwalik hills and the Kashmir Valley/Pir Panjal mountain zone. The Kashmir Valley floor is a broad intermontane plain.
records.referenceDate: NITI Aayog Roadmap for Horticulture Development in J&K, 2026

records.name: Precambrian crystalline and metamorphic rocks, Deccan Trap basalts and extensive laterites
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Goa geological report records Precambrian banded biotite gneisses, metavolcanics, phyllites, schists, greywacke and conglomerates; later intrusions include basic dykes, granites and pegmatites. Deccan Trap basalts occur in a smaller northeastern area, and lateritisation is widespread.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Goa groundwater resource assessment 2024

records.name: Quaternary alluvium over Delhi Supergroup rocks in the NCR belt
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Haryana NCR aquifer-mapping report identifies Post-Siwalik Quaternary alluvium and rocks of the Proterozoic Delhi Supergroup as the principal geological units in the studied part of Haryana.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Aquifer Mapping and Management Plan for NCR Haryana

records.name: Cenozoic sandstone, limestone and shale of the Mizo Hills
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Mizoram state profile describes the Mizo Hills as part of the Rakhine–Arakan mountain system, formed mainly of Cenozoic sandstone, limestone and shale in compact, parallel north–south ridges separated by narrow river valleys.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Mizoram groundwater resources report

records.name: Archaean crystalline basement, charnockite, gneiss, granite and younger alluvium
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Tamil Nadu hydrogeological report records formations ranging from Archaean crystalline rocks to Recent alluvium. Charnockites, gneisses and granites cover a large part of the State, with sedimentary formations and coastal/river-valley alluvium in other regions.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Groundwater Conditions in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry

records.name: Archaean gneissic complex, Proterozoic sedimentary basins and Deccan basalt
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Telangana geology chapter identifies Archaean crystalline formations and gneissic complexes as the dominant basement, with Proterozoic sedimentary and metasedimentary basin fills, Deccan basalt flows in the northwest, and younger granite, dolerite, pegmatite and quartzite intrusions.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Telangana geological and hydrogeological report

records.name: Tertiary folded sandstone and shale ranges with alluvial valley deposits
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Tripura hydrogeological report describes the State as the western fringe of the Indo-Burman fold belt, with north–south anticlinal hill ranges composed of folded Tertiary sandstone and shale, broad synclinal valleys and alluvial deposits in the structural valleys.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, State Hydrogeological Report Tripura, 2022–23

records.name: Gangetic alluvium and Himalayan geological belts
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Uttarakhand State report identifies the Gangetic Alluvial Plain and the Himalayan Mountain Belt as the principal geological domains, subdividing the latter into Outer, Lesser, Central and Tethys Himalayan units.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Dynamic Ground Water Resources of Uttarakhand State, 2023

records.name: Himalayan metamorphic and crystalline formations in the South Sikkim belt
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's aquifer-mapping report for South Sikkim includes a dedicated geology chapter and documents the district's Himalayan geological setting. This entry is district-scope and does not claim a complete lithological inventory for the entire State.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Aquifer Mapping Studies and Management Plan, South Sikkim, 2018–19

records.name: Quaternary alluvium, Tertiary sedimentary rocks and Precambrian crystalline formations
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Assam pre-monsoon 2024 bulletin groups the State's geology into unconsolidated Quaternary alluvium, semi-consolidated Tertiary siltstone, shale, claystone, sandstone and limestone, and consolidated Precambrian–Archaean crystalline and metamorphic rocks including gneiss, phyllite, schist and quartzite.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Assam Groundwater Quality Bulletin, 2024

records.name: Precambrian granite-gneiss, Vindhyan sedimentary rocks, Siwalik deposits and extensive Quaternary alluvium
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Bihar pre-monsoon 2024 bulletin records Precambrian granite and gneiss, quartzite, phyllite, slate and metabasics; Vindhyan sandstone, limestone and quartzite; Siwalik sandstone and conglomerate in West Champaran; and Quaternary alluvium covering approximately 89% of the State.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Bihar Groundwater Bulletin, 2024

records.name: Disang–Barail flysch belt and fluvio-lacustrine alluvium in the Imphal Valley
records.description: The Manipur Public Works Department's 2024 environmental assessment describes the Imphal Valley as lying within the central Disang–Barail Flysch Belt, with flat fluvio-lacustrine deposits of clay, silt and sand, bounded by thrust structures and surrounding hill ranges.
records.referenceDate: Manipur PWD, Initial Environmental Examination for Imphal Ring Road, 2024

records.name: Proterozoic Delhi Supergroup quartzite and micaceous schist overlain by older and younger alluvium
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Delhi Ground Water Year Book 2023–24 identifies quartzite interbedded with micaceous schist along the Delhi Ridge, with Quaternary older alluvium and younger Yamuna floodplain alluvium. It describes three main stratigraphic horizons across the NCT.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Delhi Ground Water Year Book 2023–24

records.name: Moraines, fluvioglacial and lacustrine sediments over hard igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Ladakh report divides the region into porous formations of moraines and fluvioglacial deposits along the Indus and fissured formations comprising hard igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks. Leh valley contains layered moraine, varved clay, silt and alluvial deposits.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Dynamic Ground Water Resources of Ladakh, 2024

records.name: Coral limestone, coral sand and reef-derived carbonate deposits
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Lakshadweep aquifer-management report describes the islands as coral reefs enclosing lagoons, with exposed hard coral limestone, coral pebbles and sands, and compact carbonate crusts. These reef-derived materials form the principal shallow aquifer across the islands.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Aquifer Mapping and Groundwater Management of Lakshadweep

records.name: Quaternary alluvial sand, silt and clay with Kandi and Sirowal piedmont deposits
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Punjab 2024 report describes the State as a predominantly alluvial plain. The alluvial deposits comprise sand, silt and clay with kankar, while the northeastern piedmont contains Kandi and Sirowal deposits grading from boulders and gravels to finer sediments.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Ground Water Resources of Punjab, 2024

records.name: Coastal alluvium, beach sands and semi-consolidated sedimentary formations
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's 2023 joint report on Tamil Nadu and the UT of Puducherry documents the regional geology of the southeastern coastal tract, including Quaternary alluvium, coastal sands, laterite, and semi-consolidated Tertiary and Cretaceous sedimentary formations. The report includes Puducherry and Karaikal monitoring units and aquifer maps.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, State Report on Groundwater Quality in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, October 2023

records.name: Kangto Peak (7,090 m)
records.description: The Arunachal Pradesh State Portal identifies Kangto at 7,090 metres as the State's highest peak. The Governor's Secretariat also confirmed the first successful summit of Kangto in November 2025.
records.referenceDate: Official Arunachal Pradesh State Portal; Governor's Secretariat, 8 December 2025

records.name: Laike Peak, Barail Range (1,959 m)
records.description: The Assam State Biodiversity Board's publication records the State's highest peak near Laike on the Barail Range at approximately 1,959 metres, overlooking the Barak Valley region.
records.referenceDate: Assam State Biodiversity Board, Amulya Jaibabaichitra, January 2017

records.name: Sonsogor Peak (1,167 m)
records.description: The Goa State Pollution Control Board's Annual Report 2014–15 identifies Sonsogor as the highest point in Goa, at approximately 1,167 metres above mean sea level.
records.referenceDate: Goa State Pollution Control Board Annual Report 2014–15

records.name: Karoh Peak, Morni Hills (1,467 m)
records.description: The Haryana State Pollution Control Board's State Action Plan identifies Karoh Peak in Panchkula district as Haryana's highest point, at approximately 1,467 metres above sea level.
records.referenceDate: Haryana State Pollution Control Board State Action Plan, 2024

records.name: Mount Iso, Senapati district
records.description: Manipur Tourism identifies Mount Iso behind Dzükou Valley in Senapati district as the highest peak in Manipur. The State Tourism portal also documents the surrounding highland landscape and access routes.
records.referenceDate: Manipur Tourism official district-wise destination profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Shivalik high point in Hoshiarpur district (approximately 900 m)
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Punjab and Chandigarh Ground Water Year Book describes the Hoshiarpur Shivalik hill belt and records a local high point of approximately 900 metres above mean sea level. The report does not name this point as a formal summit, so it is recorded as an unnamed high point rather than a named mountain peak.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Punjab and Chandigarh Ground Water Year Book 2023–24

records.name: Nun (7,135 m), Kun (7,077 m), Saser Kangri and Kang Yatse
records.description: The Ladakh Mountaineering Policy 2024 lists Nun–Kun, Saser Kangri and Kang Yatse among the region's major mountaineering peaks and records high-altitude climbing ranges from 5,000 to 7,800 metres. The Tourism Department also identifies 120 peaks open for mountaineering and trekking.
records.referenceDate: Ladakh Mountaineering Policy, 2024

records.name: No distinct named mountain peak within the UT boundary
records.description: The Chandigarh Administration describes the UT as gently sloping plains at the foothills of the Shivalik range, with an altitude of approximately 304–365 metres. The official profile does not identify a named mountain summit within Chandigarh's 114-square-kilometre boundary; nearby Shivalik peaks lie outside the UT.
records.referenceDate: Chandigarh Administration official General Information and Topography profile accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: Delhi Ridge (Aravalli outcrop; no separately named mountain summit in the official profile)
records.description: Delhi Tourism and the Delhi Forest Department identify the Delhi Ridge as the northern extension of the ancient Aravalli range, divided into Northern, Southern, Central and South-Central Ridge zones. The official profile documents the ridge as Delhi's principal rocky upland rather than naming a single mountain summit.
records.referenceDate: Delhi Tourism and Delhi Forest Department profiles accessed 31 October 2026

records.name: No mountain peaks: low coral atolls and reef islands
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's Lakshadweep aquifer-mapping report describes the islands as low-lying coral reef formations, with coral limestone, coral sand and shallow freshwater lenses. The UT has no natural mountain peaks; its highest landforms are low coral islands and reef structures.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Aquifer Mapping and Groundwater Management of Lakshadweep

records.name: No major natural mountain peak: coastal plain and low-relief terrain
records.description: The Central Ground Water Board's joint Tamil Nadu and Puducherry report describes the UT's physiography as a low-lying coastal plain with alluvial and sedimentary formations. No distinct natural mountain peak is identified within the UT in the cited regional geology report.
records.referenceDate: Central Ground Water Board, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry report, 2023
